newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon offers olive branch to striking teacher.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon offers olive branch to striking teacher.

text.p: The Cameroon government, anxious to put the disrupted 1996/97 school year back on track, has offered striking teachers a range of allowances.
But the teachers unions who launched the pay strike call to coincide with the start of the school year on September 12 say the offer does not go far enough.
A government decree published on Saturday offered special allowances ranging from 5,000 CFA to 12,500 CFA to primary school teachers.

"The offer is a good thing but it is not enough given the mass of problems that teachers and schools face in Cameroon," Njoh Mbongue Luison, general secretary of the National Organisation of Teachers of Cameroon (ONEC) told Reuters.
"Don't forget that our salaries were cut by 70 percent in 1993 and that the state owes us two months of backpay from the same year," he added.
"Classrooms are packed. How can you teach 120 children who for the most part have neither exercise book nor text book?"
The World Bank and the United Nations and other aid groups are keen to boost primary education in Africa so more children gain reading, writing and counting skills essential to developing economies.
Cameroon, like many African countries, is trying to squeeze its bloated civil service pay bill in line with reforms recommended by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
